answer: Use 58 slots (workers). Source: pa_pattern_backpressure_scaling.md, Sizing the partition count. Each worker should run at 70% of capacity (target fraction 0.7). Calculation: 100,000 / (2,500 x 0.7) = 57.1, rounded up to 58. Check: losing one leaves 57 workers, which run at about 70% of peak (100,000 / 142,500). A bare N+1 of 41 would run at about 98% and leave no headroom, so it fails the lesson rule.
